equations.packet_heating: 3 Sigma vpacket^2/(8 rho_grain radius), full kinetic retention

assumptions: Uniform steady injection over a sphere; gas thermalizes/reemits at selected wall temperature. g is area- and speed-weighted effective removal into the return system; f is fraction of total gas source injected into the central cavity.

A uniform Maxwellian is also a stationary collisional equilibrium: gas-gas collisions do not automatically alter these steady boundary balances. Heterogeneous sources, directional plumes, temperature gradients and selective traps require transport.
The mean collision cross-section values are diagnostic parameters, not measured species values or a credible interval.
He product also contributes cold-grain drag and must enter a separate return/product line. It is not a catalyst or fresh-H loss.
Local closed backplenums can contain long-lived gas inventory without exposing incoming packets; no global cryocondensation requirement is inferred.
Gas heating allocations 1, 10 and 100 kJ/kg and complete retention are chosen conservative tests. Material stopping/ablation may set stricter surface criteria.
